[LGRA.5.2] The grammar admits an optional `schema_lifecycle`
clause (`scope <value>`) **after** the type name. The four
scope values (`explicit`, `logical`, `ttl <time_expr>`,
`activation`), the `ambient` modifier `logical` and `ttl` admit, and their
semantics live at [LSCP.1.5] and [LSCP.1.7]. When the clause is
omitted, the schema defaults to `scope explicit` per
[LSCP.1.4]. The `ttl` form takes a mandatory duration, a
`time_expr` ([LGRA.2.8.2]), whose value becomes the schema's default
per-fact TTL per [LFAC.1.3.3] / [RDSC.5.3.3]. The compiler must refuse
a `ttl` whose duration is zero, written as `0_s` or as a constant whose
value is zero ([LGRA.2.8.11]), with `DS_VALIDATE_TTL_ZERO`: a fact
whose TTL is zero would be retracted before any rule could observe it.
